🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk appetite snapped back hard. Bitcoin ripped above $81K as traders shrugged off back-to-back Fed and BoJ hikes, while Washington's regulators pressed ahead without Congress and security headlines kept stacking up. 🚀 Bitcoin Rips Above $81K as Rate-Hike Fear Evaporates Bitcoin climbed almost 6% in 24 hours and printed above $81,000 — its first move over $80K since Sept. 7 — after the market absorbed a Federal Reserve hike, a Bank of Japan increase to 1.25% and the collapse of the CLARITY Act without breaking. Ether added 7.3%, XRP 8.9% and Solana 12.7%, while Strategy, Gemini and Coinbase shares all booked double-digit gains. Read full story ⚖️ CFTC Sends Its Own Crypto Rulebook to the White House Two days after the Senate blocked the CLARITY Act 49–50, the CFTC filed "Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets" with the White House budget office, moving ahead on existing statutory authority. The agency also published a no-action letter letting passive software providers — including some crypto wallet interfaces — connect users to regulated derivatives markets without registering as introducing brokers. More details 🇪🇺 Lagarde Personally Blocked Binance's EU License, WSJ Reports ECB President Christine Lagarde intervened to stop Binance's MiCA authorization in Greece, reportedly urging Athens not to sign off on an application the national regulator had already deemed complete. The concern: the world's largest exchange accelerating dollar-stablecoin adoption in Europe and undercutting the digital euro. Binance pulled the filing in June, forfeiting passport access to 450 million EU residents. Read more 🛢️ US Sanctions the Iranian Exchange Behind Hormuz Bitcoin Tolls OFAC designated Tehran-based BitBank, alleging it moved hundreds of millions of dollars in bitcoin to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and processed the "safe passage" fees Iran charges tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz. Treasury also named the exchange's software developer and three associates of sanctioned financier Babak Zanjani, freezing their US-held property.
